chapter_title: Concerning the First Man and the Ambassador and the Ship; what they resemble.
chapter_note: A chain of five similes mapping major cosmic redeemers (First Man, Ship of the Day/Great Spirit, Living Spirit, Ambassador) onto human analogies is the dominant layer. The only clear later addition is the closing exhortation to disciples in direct second-person application voice. The opening paragraph contains a brief hagiographic dialogue-attribution that must be stripped to recover the older teaching unit.

paragraphs.core_text: The First [Man] is like a great distinguished man whose treasure has been taken away from him. He came to pursue his treasure. This is how the [First] Man too came after his sons from the heights, so that he might redeem them and retrieve his treasure, which had been scattered amongst his enemies.
paragraphs.removed_material: Removed the dialogue/frame attribution “Once again he speaks:” (hagiographic/editorial container).
paragraphs.temporal_note: The simile itself stays within the cosmic system (First Man, sons/treasure, enemies, redemption) in impersonal explanatory mode; only the prefixed speech formula marks later framing.

paragraphs.core_text: Once again, [he is like a man] whose two sons were taken away from him by [ ... He] came out toward them to redeem them. Again, this is how the First Man [ ... ] shines in the heights because of his two sons, who were separated from him. They are his living soul that exist in two powers, which makes four.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Systematic cosmological accounting (sons/living soul/powers, numerical relation) presented as a simile without institutional targeting or exhortation; no citation or pastoral address.

paragraphs.core_text: Once again, the ship [of the day] is like a great spear [ ... ... The Great Spirit too, which is in it, is like a wise [crafts]man who might beautify and set aright [all] the armour for war.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Cosmic entity-to-object correspondence (Ship of the Day/Great Spirit ↔ spear/craftsman; beautifying/ordering) remains internal to the mythic-cosmological system.

paragraphs.core_text: Once again, the Living Spirit is like a combatant who might go towards a king's son who has been taken prisoner of war, and he redeems him from the hands of his enemies.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Pure redemption simile (Living Spirit’s function) with no shift into contemporary institutions or audience instruction; characteristic core explanatory voice.

paragraphs.core_text: [The Amba]ssador too is like a great man [ ... ] because of the treasure [ ... ] hand of his prisoners [ ... ] these light powers [ ... ... the] sons and their soul, so that they would [ ... ... (the soul) might] be brought forth in the land wherein it was imprisoned.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Despite lacunae, the sentence structure indicates another cosmological redemption simile (Ambassador, light powers, soul’s release) with no frame formulas or pastoral application.

Direct second-person exhortation (“You yourselves must…”) and goal-oriented moral application (be purifiers/redeemers, be counted worthy) shifts from describing cosmic mechanisms to instructing an audience—typical later pastoral/application layer.
